name: Jason Rau Ankle Lock System
summary: Jason Rau’s Dynamic Ankle Locks groups ankle-attack study by grips, leg positions, opponent posture and secondary options.
description: Locate ankle-lock material for seated, kneeling and standing situations in Jason Rau’s course.
overview: An ankle-lock question can concern the initial connection, a change in the opponent’s posture, or the next option after the attack stalls. Rau’s three-volume outline separates those areas and names both submission and back-taking alternatives.

includes: Volume 1 addresses grips and leg positions; Volume 2 distinguishes posture-specific finishing situations.
Volume 3 lists heel-hook, bear-trap and back-taking alternatives.
limits: Aoki locks and heel hooks are explicitly included; the title does not describe a straight-ankle-only syllabus.

start_here.title: Sort the posture-specific lessons
start_here.task: In the public Volume 2 outline, mark the seated and kneeling sections separately. Choose the posture that matches the problem you want to study, then check whether the selected heading names an ankle lock or an Aoki option. With course access, compare the demonstrated starting positions before combining your notes.
start_here.section: Volume 2: Butterfly Hook Vs Kneeling Opponent (16:13); Y Guard Vs Kneeling Opponent (19:50).

flashcards.question: Which opponent postures should an ankle-lock observation log distinguish?
flashcards.answer: Keep seated, kneeling and standing examples separate. Rau’s outline names these situations separately, so observations from one should not silently stand in for another.
